judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the definition of health care provider ... is interpreted to include subsidiaries of holding companies of the named insured' is syntactically muddled — it is unclear whether it captures subsidiaries, holding companies, or both, and it purports to rewrite a statutory definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the exclusion in c100 across the corporate group described in c020 and c085, so which listed insureds are caught is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-condition contingency ('adheres to the definition', paid an assessment, granted a separate set of limits) and the phrase 'is nevertheless disallowed coverage by the Patients Compensation Fund' are convoluted and turn on a third party's decision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises cover 'directly over the underlying insurance listed in this policy and identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes', but Item 7 identifies no such policy, and it cuts against c082 and c100.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves 'appropriate' wholly undefined and unilateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same formula in c122 and sits against Condition 1 (c044) and the Pay Plan (c097-c098), which state the premium as fixed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies 'Form No. 035(12/87) Professional Services Excluded' whereas the form actually attached is 035 WI (1/94) — a cross-reference error in a clause that switches coverage on and off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its interaction with c082-c083 (which already carve out entities not subject to the Fund) and with c100-c102 leaves the professional-services position genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative words are only 'the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy are amended', followed by a statutory recitation that states no amendment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This umbrella policy contains no Hospital Professional Liability coverage part (that is the separate HPP policy in Item 7), and Endorsement No. 5 (c111) declares this form null and void, so its status is doubly problematic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity is payable only 'if it is determined that payment of said loss shall be rendered under this policy', a circular condition, and 'necessarily incurred' is evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises legal expenses that the Ultimate Net Loss definition (c033) expressly excludes and interacts with the Other Insurance clause (c052) that generates such disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Labelled an exclusion yet it obliges the company to pay one-third of a trebled award, and it defines 'damages' as excluding plaintiff's legal fees only 'for purposes of this exclusion' — an awkward mix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 (c111) deletes Form 009-133 and declares it null and void, yet the form remains in the endorsement schedule and in the policy as issued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stated effective date is the policy inception, consistent with the endorsement's own heading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the policy limits in Item 2' although limits appear in Item 3 (Item 2 is the policy period), and the additional premium is left blank ('$ ___').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state $18,000,000 each occurrence and $9,000,000 aggregate while this endorsement states $20,000,000/$20,000,000, and the aggregate proviso in c013/c084 keys off the declared figures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the endorsement is effective on inception, though the deletions it introduces are dated later in the year.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'deleted from the policy and considered null and void' is unambiguous in its operation, though it identifies one form by number alone (009-133) and one with an edition date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both deleted forms (c107 Trebled Damages and c105 Policy Territory 10/92) remain in the endorsement schedule and in the assembled policy, so the instrument as a whole contains provisions the endorsement voids.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line attachment of a replacement form; no term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The replacement (c113) again amends a Hospital Professional Liability coverage part that this umbrella policy does not contain, and the form is not listed on the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its predecessor it recites a statute without stating any substantive amendment to territory, and the recited text is mis-cited ('s.446.37' for s.146.37).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to amend a Hospital Professional Liability coverage part absent from this policy and sits against the unqualified Territory clause (c014) and the professional services exclusion (c082).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'effective on the inception date' language conflicts mildly with the endorsement's stated effective date of 07/08/1996.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'Form 0098-052' — a typographical rendering of 009-052 — to add one entity; otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It enlarges the Named Insured list in c085, which matters for the Cross Suits Endorsement (c059) and the cancellation-notice deeming rule (c086).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the endorsement takes effect on the policy inception date while the endorsement's own effective date is 01/01/1997, a discrepancy of some months.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'CMG - Brown Deer Campus' is named as a Named Insured although a campus is a location rather than a person or organization, which the Named Insured definition requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c020 (Named Insured means a person or organization named in the declarations), c085's list and c119's renaming of the parent, and its mid-term date conflicts with c116's inception-date language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It backdates to inception although the endorsement was issued in November 1997, after the policy period expired.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It changes the named insured from 'Children's Health Systems, Inc.' to 'Children's Health System, Inc.', a one-letter correction whose intent (correction versus substitution of entity) is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations, every endorsement heading and c085 still use the plural form, so the instrument as a whole names the insured inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds two campuses to Form 009-052; the same person/organization problem as c117 arises for 'Campus' entries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the Named Insured list (c085) after the policy period on its face, and campuses are not 'organizations' within c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' is a compound and circular identification, and 'this coverage' is not specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement is headed to policy HPP-1996-4104-00, not this umbrella, yet it appears in the policy and interacts with the professional services exclusion carve-out (c083) and the Item 7 schedule of $1,000,000 underlying limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves both the trigger ('if the need ... is ever required') and the amount undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c103 and sits against the fixed premium in Condition 1 (c044) and the Pay Plan Endorsement (c097-c098).
